Typical reflux symptoms

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 34-year-old woman reports recurrent burning behind the sternum and sour fluid reaching her mouth after large meals, especially when she lies down. She has no dysphagia or bleeding. Which diagnosis best fits this symptom pattern?

  1. Acute appendicitis
  2. Gastroesophageal reflux disease
  3. Achalasia
  4. Acute pancreatitis
  5. Biliary colic
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Gastroesophageal reflux disease

Heartburn and regurgitation associated with meals and recumbency are typical reflux symptoms.

Understanding the options

Gastroesophageal reflux disease
Heartburn and regurgitation associated with meals and recumbency are typical reflux symptoms.
Achalasia
Progressive swallowing difficulty and retained food are more characteristic.
Acute pancreatitis
This usually produces sustained severe epigastric pain rather than recurrent sour regurgitation.
Biliary colic
This commonly causes episodic right upper quadrant or epigastric pain, not sour reflux.
Acute appendicitis
The location and meal-related regurgitation do not fit appendicitis.
